rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=160, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the iter-2 BEST config (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001), NOT iter-3's regressed lambda 0.003. ONE KNOB: tv_iterations 120->160 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) -- the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) -- REGRESSED, over-smoothed (lambda-up is exhausted). The two prior levers are SPENT: tv_clip_max is at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] (clip exhausted), and tv_lambda-up regressed in iter-3 (denoise-strength exhausted). The remaining untried lever is tv_iterations: it has been FROZEN at 120 for all 3 prior iters, deliberately conservative to protect the 20-min wall. OPPORTUNITY: is hr 0.205 ITERATIONS-LIMITED (the TV gradient descent has not fully converged at 120 steps, so the recon still has residual data-term error the schedule has not driven out) or is it at the TV REGULARIZATION CEILING (120 iters is already converged and 0.205 hr / ~0.924 SSIM is the structural TV limit on real Mayo LDCT)? FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: oversizing tv_iterations blows the HARD 20-min (1200s) wall on the 214-slice val pass. HYPOTHESIS: 33% more TV gradient-descent steps (120->160) from the iter-2 BEST config converge the recon further, lowering val_rmse below 7.857e-4 so hr rises above 0.205364 (the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual). FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression at 160 iters), TV is at its regularization ceiling on Mayo (~0.924 SSIM / 0.205 hr) and 120 iters was already converged -- the iters lever is exhausted too, and the next probe would be tv_lr (finer convergence per step) or accept the structural TV ceiling. BUDGET: the cost model is T(n)=overhead + n*c_step. From iter-2's 928.5s at 120 iters and the iter-1 per-slice-iter rate (~0.018 s/slice-iter * 214 slices = 3.85 s/TV-iter), fixed overhead (214-slice load+FBP+per-iter scoring) ~= 466s. n=160 -> T ~= 466 + 160*3.85 ~= 1083s = 90% of the 1200s budget (~117s margin). Robustness: even at +10% step-cost variance (GPU contention) n=160 lands ~1144s, still under the wall; n=180 was REJECTED because at +10% variance it goes over (1229s). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.
